title: In re Hanninen, Winfred, BIIA Dec., 50,653 (1979)
text:
Hanninen, Winfred
OCCUPATIONAL DISEASE (RCW 51.08.140)
Successive insurers
The insurer on the risk for an occupational disease claim (hearing loss) on the date of
compensable disability is responsible for the full costs of the claim if the employment at
that time continued to be "of a kind" which contributes to hearing loss, whether or not it
added any specific percentage amount to the worker's hearing loss. ….In re
Winfred Hanninen, BIIA Dec., 50,653 (1979)

18 This is an appeal filed by the employer, Longview Fibre Company, on October 3, 1977, from
19
an order of the Department of Labor and Industries dated August 4, 1977, which adhered to a prior
20
21 order closing this claim with a permanent partial disability award of 21.2% complete loss of hearing
22
in both ears, and determined that this occupational disease claim is the self-insured employer's
23
24 responsibility. SUSTAINED.

DECISION
26
27 Pursuant to RCW 51.52.104 and RCW 51.52.106, this matter is before the Board for review
28
and decision on a timely Petition for Review filed by the employer to a Proposed Decision and
29
30 Order issued by a hearing examiner for this Board on July 31, 1978, in which the order of the
31
Department dated August 4, 1977 was sustained.
32
33 The Board has reviewed the evidentiary rulings of the hearing examiner and finds that no
34
prejudicial error was committed and said rulings are hereby affirmed.
35
36 The issues presented by this appeal and the evidence presented by the parties are very
37
adequately discussed in our hearing examiner's Proposed Decision and Order.
38
39 Four issues were raised by this appeal: (1) Whether an occupational noise-induced hearing
40
loss can legally constitute an occupational disease under our Act; (2) Whether this claimant's
41
42 hearing loss was in fact caused by the occupational noise exposure and is therefore compensable;
43
(3) Whether the permanent partial disability rating of 21.2% binaural hearing impairment was a
44
45 reasonable and correct award for the occupationally-caused hearing loss; and (4) Whether financial
46
responsibility for this occupational disease claim should be borne by Longview Fibre Company as a
47

1
self-insured employer, or by the Department, i.e., the State Fund, which carried Longview Fibre's
2
industrial insurance coverage prior to January 1, 1974.
3
4
As to issues (1), (2), and (3), we readily answer each question in the affirmative, as did our
5
hearing examiner. The Proposed Decision and Order set forth the reasons for so deciding very
6
7
fully and logically, and we incorporate all that discussion as our own.
8
As to issue (4), we likewise concur in the hearing examiner's decision; and conclude that this
9
10
claim is Longview Fibre Company's responsibility in its self-insured capacity. We note that counsel
11
for the employer included in his Petition for Review a request for oral argument on the issue of
12
13
responsibility for this claim as between the State Fund and the self-insured employer. We have
14
determined no need for this, inasmuch as this same issue has been previously reviewed and
15
16
exhaustively discussed by the Board, in the case of Delbert Monroe, docket No. 49,698, our
17
Decision and Order of 7/24/78. We refer to and incorporate our discussion of the issue in that case,
18
19
and note that it is in basic accord with the examiner's well-reasoned analysis in the instant case.
20
Particularly, we refer to our discussion on pages 6 and 7 of the Monroe case, showing that this
21
22
employer did not pay any premiums for this type of case while insured with the State Fund prior to
23
becoming self-insured. We adhere to the general principle requiring the insurer on the risk at the
24
25
date of compensability to bear the monetary responsibility for these long-developing occupational
26
disease claims.
27
28
After consideration of the Proposed Decision and Order and the employer's Petition for
29
Review filed thereto, and a careful review of the entire record before us, we are persuaded that the
30
31
Proposed Decision and Order is supported by the preponderance of the evidence and is correct as
32
a matter of law.
33
34
The hearing examiner's proposed findings, conclusions and order are hereby adopted as this
35
Board's findings, conclusions and order and are incorporated herein by this reference.

citation: In re Hanninen, Winfred, BIIA Dec., 50,653 (1979)
headnote: The insurer on the risk for an occupational disease claim (hearing loss) on the date of compensable disability is responsible for the full costs of the claim if the employment at that time continued to be "of a kind" which contributes to hearing loss, whether or not it added any specific percentage amount to the worker's hearing loss.
